newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alchemists carousels and racoons star in Mexico vote.
newsitem.headline: Alchemists carousels and racoons star in Mexico vote.

text.p: Mexico has developed a colourful vocabulary of election terms over the years, appropriate for a country where the cleanliness of the electoral process has often been the biggest issue.
Announcement of the official results has more often than not been accompanied by cries of foul play by opposition parties as the Instituional Revolutionary Party (PRI) cruises to yet another victory.

The PRI has held power for 68 unbroken years here and hopes to prolong that record in Sunday's national elections. The government and the newly independent Federal Electoral Institute have said these will be the cleanest elections ever.
A brief list of terms follows:
Acarreados: Supporters bused in to rallies in return for free food, drink, T-shirts and baseball caps with a party logo.
Alquimista electoral. An "alchemist" who turns unpromising election results into numerous PRI seats in Congress.
Carro completo. "All aboard." When a party wins every single seat up for grabs at an election, as the PRI did in the Senate until 1988.
Carrusel. Party members go on a "merry-go-round" of polling booths, voting in each one with the connivance of corrupt polling officials.
Hueso: A "bone" in the form of a government job or political post tossed some one's way in return for services rendered.
Fantasmas. "Ghosts". Registered voters who are in fact dead, registered at unlikely addresses such as statues or monuments, or in improbably large numbers at a small home.
Mapaches. "Racoons" or mysterious figures who steal ballot boxes filled with opposition votes on election night:
Periodicazo: Newspaper advertisments blasting opposition parties and candidates. Paid for by organisations no one has heard of.
Rasurado del padron: "Shaving" the electoral roll by eliminating voters who are known opposition activists.
Raton Loco: When only PRI members know where polling stations are. The opposition run around like "crazy mice" looking for them and then give up.
Tacos: Pre-endorsed ballots rolled up like tacos and stuffed into ballot boxes.
Urnas panzonas: "Pregnant" ballot boxes that contain ready endorsed ballot papers before voting begins.
Zapatazo: A polling station with no independent scrutiny where the PRI wins 100 percent, or more, of the registered voters. As in a game of dominos, one player wins while another keeps all the chips.
